subject: SOC2 artifact exchange: signer rotation + evidence latency SLAs
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@bluecrestgrc.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@redprobe.com>, audit-team@clientco.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 artifact exchange / onboarding window

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for making time on the call yesterday. BlueCrest is onboarding a set of customers that want direct artifact exchange from vendor GRC integrations (S3/SFTP/secure upload). Two things we need to confirm before we can move on: signer rotation for automated artifact transmission (we need a defined schedule and key rotation process) and an SLA on artifact delivery latency — our customers require that uploaded artifacts be visible in the audit queue within 24 hours.

Can you share Redwood's current signer/key rotation cadence and the typical end-to-end latency we should model for SOC2 artifacts (ingest → indexing → available via evidence API)? Also attaching a short manifest template we usually ask partners to fill out.

Attachment: evidence_manifest_v1.csv (CSV, 12KB)

Looking to align next steps with Tom (Red Probe) who will run a dry-run pen-test artifact pull next month.

Cheers,
Samantha Ortiz
Partnerships Lead, BlueCrest GRC
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@bluecrestgrc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 artifact exchange / onboarding window

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front:
- Signer/key rotation: we support monthly key rotation for partner upload keys; for tighter reg requirements we can move to a 14-day rotation with automated rotation hooks (we'll push a rotation webhook to your endpoint).
- Latency: typical ingest -> indexed -> evidence API availability for artifact bundles is 2–6 hours in our hosted environment; in Dedicated/Private it can vary (we should scope). For your 24-hour SLA that's comfortably inside the envelope, but we'll document worst-case during heavy ingest windows.

Proposed immediate plan:
1) Karthik will send SFTP + signed-upload instructions and an ephemeral key rotation playbook.
2) Marcus will run a 1TB dry-run ingest on a sandbox and report realistic 95th/99th percentile availability numbers.
3) BlueCrest completes the manifest and returns (Samantha), then Tom executes the dry-run pull with Red Probe.

Looping in Laura for any procurement/BAA redlines that might block automated artifact exchange.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

--

Samantha/Evelyn —

Attached are the SFTP instructions and a short runbook for key rotation. Notes:
- We recommend using a rotating SSH key pair per partner; rotation can be automated via our partner API (POST /partners/{id}/rotate-key).
- For immediate dry-run please use the sandbox bucket url in the Drive link and the temporary credentials below (will expire in 72 hours).
- Ingest pipeline: artifacts land in a staging shard, go through validation + dedupe, then are indexed. Large bundles (>.5GB) are chunked and indexed in parallel — that’s where 95th/99th latency can increase. Expect 2–6 hours for typical bundles; heavy concurrent uploads can see up to 12 hours at worst in hosted.

Temporary credentials (sandbox):
- user: bluecrest-dryrun
- host: sftp.sandbox.redwood.com
- port: 2222
- key: (ephemeral key provided in the Drive link)

Attachment: redwood-sftp-instructions.md (text, 4KB)

Will follow up with a short report after the Marcus dry-run.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@bluecrestgrc.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 artifact exchange / onboarding window

Samantha —

I kicked off the 1TB sandbox ingest this morning against the sandbox SFTP. Preliminary numbers after the first 120GB: median availability ~3h10m; 95th ~5h45m; a few outliers hit 9–10h when concurrent indexing jobs spiked. I’ll collect full figures and an indexed-timeline CSV by EOD tomorrow.

Two operational asks:
- Can BlueCrest confirm whether artifacts will be pushed as compressed tarballs or as discrete files? That affects indexing parallelism.
- We need a signed BAA amendment for automated artifact sharing; attaching the DocuSign request. Laura — can your team kick off the procurement/BAA review?

Attachment: docsign_baa_request.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@bluecrestgrc.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 artifact exchange / onboarding window

Hi all —

Procurement/Legal here. I reviewed the DocuSign BAA request; one narrow redline around data retention language and one ask about subprocessor notifications. Samantha — can you confirm BlueCrest's retention default and whether you will notify partners when third-party processors are added? I can get the amended BAA back in DocuSign within 48 hours once we have that.

On the technical side: compressed tarballs are fine (prefer gzipped chunks). Marcus — once you finish the full ingest report, please include a short matrix listing chunk-size vs observed latency so we can set a recommended default for partners.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Procurement Counsel
Redwood Inference
